why: One configuration source. The audit (F03) found compiler/targets/tnca-sim-v0.1.json describing a four-tile system with capabilities.sfu=true while rtl/tile/tnca_tile.v elaborated its core with .HAS_SFU(0). A compiler reading that target would emit an SFU instruction the machine raises ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION on. The target must describe the *elaborated instance*, not some module's default, and the only way to keep that true is for the parameters, the target JSON, the capability expectations and the test command to come from one place.

core-sim.description: One core, two Role Contexts. What tb/core/tb_tnca_core.v elaborates, and what every single-core compiler test targets.

platform_binding.what: the testbench that reads this profile's capabilities back out of the hardware

core-4r.description: One core, four Role Contexts, half the logical vector registers each so the physical file is the same size. compiler_overview.md sec 15 C4's P+M0+M1+E profile.

platform_binding.what: the testbench that reads this profile's capabilities back out of the hardware

system-2x2.description: Four tiles in a 2x2 mesh, two Role Contexts per core, four NUCA slices, DRAM behind them. What tb/top/tb_tnca_top.v elaborates.
system-2x2.note: HAS_SFU is 0 here and that is the correct profile, not a defect to be papered over. The contract is explicit: the system's SFU stays off rather than being switched on to remove the inconsistency. What was wrong was the target claiming otherwise.

platform_binding.what: the testbench that reads this profile's capabilities back out of the hardware

core-vrf-sync-v1.description: The same single core with the banked, synchronous, finite-port vector register file. Architecturally identical to core-sim -- same ISA, same register capacity, same two role contexts -- so a difference in a result is a difference in implementation. R3 v2's candidate.

platform_binding.what: the testbench that reads this profile's capabilities back out of the hardware

core-xpose-v1.description: core-sim with the transfer engine's transposed write (ISA sec 9E mod[5]) elaborated: HAS_TENSOR_XPOSE=1 and capability tensor_transpose. Otherwise identical to core-sim, so a difference in a result is the feature. R38 S1-07's first three-layer change.

platform_binding.what: the testbench that reads this profile's capabilities back out of the hardware

supported_topologies.note: Nothing else is supported. rtl/noc/tnca_core_ni.v computes a 2-bit home and rtl/tnca_top.v fixes N_W=2, so raising NX/NY does not produce a correct 16-slice home or a wide enough source tag (audit F05). An unsupported topology must fail at configuration time rather than elaborate into a machine that misroutes.

bench_args_note: Every Role Context the profile defines is launched. NUM_ROLES reports the count this LAUNCH activated (ISA sec 5.1), not the core's architectural maximum, so a capability read-back that started one context would disagree with a target describing two -- and would be right to. A profile's capabilities are the capabilities of the whole profile.
platform_binding_note: Phase 3.6 section 3.1 separates a compile target from a platform binding: a target describes the ISA, the ABI, the capabilities and the resources, and 'cannot be equated with a particular simulator executable or a particular board'. The bench below is a VERIFICATION binding -- which testbench exercises this profile's capabilities on this host -- and it is deliberately not copied into the generated target the compiler reads. The DEVICE binding lives in python/tnca/device.py, which is the one the runtime uses.
